arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: General Verrilli argued that military honors sustain core national values.
He stated that Congress has a long tradition of protecting the honors system.
Mr. Libby argued that the Stolen Valor Act criminalizes pure speech.
He noted that the law punishes lies regardless of the context or audience.

paragraphs: The government seeks to uphold the law to protect the integrity of military honors.
The defendant seeks to strike down the law to protect free speech from government punishment.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary between government regulation and individual expression. It determines whether citizens can speak falsely about military service without facing federal prison. The outcome shapes the scope of free speech protections in public discourse.
